phases.name: Target Market Assessment and Fair Value Check
phases.description: A personal customer selects a Premier Account upgrade in the mobile app which includes travel insurance underwritten by a third-party insurer (Aviva). SVC-004 (Insurance Distribution Service) performs the FCA PROD target market assessment: verifying the customer fits the identified target market (age 18-75, UK resident, frequent traveller). A fair value assessment confirms the insurance premium provides adequate cover relative to cost. The customer is presented with the IPID (Insurance Product Information Document) and Key Features Document per ICOBS.
entry_conditions: Customer is authenticated in mobile app
Premier Account product is available to the customer's segment
exit_conditions: Target market assessment completed — customer within target market
Fair value assessment completed — product provides fair value
IPID and Key Features Document presented to customer

phases.name: Customer Acceptance and Policy Binding
phases.description: Customer reviews IPID and Key Features Document and accepts. SVC-004 binds the insurance policy with the underwriter (Aviva) via an API call. A policy number is issued. SVC-004 creates an InsurancePolicy record. EVT-167 InsurancePolicyBound is published.
entry_conditions: Target market and fair value assessments complete
IPID and Key Features Document presented
exit_conditions: Certificate of insurance sent to customer

phases.name: Account Fee Update and Consumer Duty Recording
phases.description: SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core) updates the current account to Premier Account with the monthly fee reflecting the insurance bundle. The Consumer Duty evidence trail is saved: target market assessment result, fair value assessment result, IPID acknowledgement, and policy binding confirmation. Customer can view and cancel the insurance policy within the bank's app.
exit_conditions: Current account upgraded to Premier with insurance bundle fee
Customer can manage insurance in app

happy_path.description: Customer selects Premier Account → target market assessment passed → fair value check passed → IPID presented → customer accepts → policy bound with Aviva → account fee updated → Consumer Duty evidence saved.

alternative_paths.name: Customer Outside Target Market — Product Not Offered
alternative_paths.description: Target market assessment identifies customer is outside the defined target market (e.g. customer is over 75 or has a pre-existing condition that excludes them from standard travel insurance). Insurance product not offered. Alternative products presented if available.
alternative_paths.diverges_at: PH-136: Target market assessment returns outside_target_market

design_decisions.decision: InsurancePolicy is owned by SVC-004 (Insurance Distribution Service, CAP-001). The account fee update is triggered by EVT-167 consumed by SVC-001 (same CAP-001) — intra-capability communication.
design_decisions.rationale: SVC-004 is promoted to its own sub-capability (CAP-001.06) but remains within CAP-001's boundary. SVC-001 and SVC-004 are intra-capability peers.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Cross-capability event for account fee update — rejected as SVC-001 and SVC-004 are both within CAP-001.

design_decisions.decision: The underwriter binding call (SVC-004 → Aviva) is an external API call to a third-party insurer. This is modelled as an internal SVC-004 action, not as a separate service in the architectural model.
design_decisions.rationale: Aviva is an external counterparty, not an internal bank service. The boundary is at SVC-004 — it manages the underwriter relationship.
